sourcedFrom: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 (2026)
cleanIntro:
The SIG P385 is a striker-fired 9mm pistol built around a fire control unit that sits in an interchangeable grip module. It comes with or without a manual safety, some carry a loaded chamber indicator or a magazine disconnect, and some slides have a compensator built in.

The field strip is a takedown lever with the slide locked back: no trigger press, and the lever will not turn with a magazine in the gun. It leaves the slide, the barrel, the recoil spring guide assembly and the frame. DEEP CLEAN carries what SIG publishes beyond that: the magazine apart, and the fire control unit out of the grip module. SIG says to clean and lubricate before or after the pistol is fired, or every 500 rounds, in normal conditions.

steps.title: Know which P385 you have
steps.action: Look for three things. A manual safety lever, on both sides of the frame. A loaded chamber indicator at the top of the slide. And whether the trigger is dead with the magazine out, which is how a magazine disconnect behaves. Do not touch the trigger to find out — that check belongs in the function check, on a proven-empty pistol.
steps.prose: SIG sells this pistol with and without each of them. None of the three replaces looking into the chamber.
steps.quote: Some models feature a magazine disconnect mechanism which mechanically blocks the movement of the trigger bar, preventing the trigger from being pressed to the rear unless a magazine is inserted.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 8.3 Principal Safety Features, printed p.24

steps.title: Safety on, muzzle safe, magazine out
steps.action: If your P385 has a manual safety, rotate the lever up. Point the muzzle in a safe direction, keep your finger off the trigger, and press the magazine catch to take the magazine out. Put it and any ammunition out of reach.
steps.prose: The slide still works with the manual safety on, so it can stay on through the clearing.
steps.quote: 1. If equipped, engage the manual safety. 2. Point the muzzle in a safe direction. 3. Release the magazine.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 9.2 Unloading and Clearing the Pistol, printed p.36
steps.warn: REMOVING THE MAGAZINE FROM THE FIREARM DOES NOT PREVENT A CHAMBERED ROUND FROM BEING FIRED UNLESS THE FIREARM IS EQUIPPED WITH A MAGAZINE DISCONNECT MECHANISM.

steps.title: Slide locked back, then check three places twice
steps.action: Pull the slide all the way back, watching for a round to come out, and push the slide catch lever up to hold it open. Look at and feel the chamber, the breech face and the magazine well. Then check all three again.
steps.prose: SIG names the breech face as well as the chamber: a round or a case can hang on the extractor there with the chamber itself empty.
steps.quote:
6. Visually and physically check the firearm is clear of all ammunition twice by inspecting the
chamber (1), breech face (2), and magazine well (3).
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 9.2 Unloading and Clearing the Pistol, printed p.36

steps.title: Slide locked to the rear, no magazine in the gun
steps.action: With the pistol cleared, make sure the slide is still locked back on the slide catch lever. If it has gone forward, pull it back and push the slide catch lever up until it holds.
steps.prose: The takedown lever turns only from here: slide locked back and the magazine out. That is the design keeping you from taking the pistol apart loaded.
steps.quote: Lock the slide to rear by pulling the slide rearward and pushing up on the slide catch lever.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.1 Pistol Disassembly, step 2, printed p.57

steps.title: Takedown lever clockwise to its stop
steps.action: Turn the takedown lever on the left side of the frame clockwise until it stops, perpendicular to the slide. Use your fingers.
steps.prose: If it will not turn, the slide is not locked fully back or a magazine is in the well. Turning it lowers the sear, so the trigger is not pressed at any point in this strip.
steps.quote: 3. Rotate the takedown lever clockwise until it stops.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.1 Pistol Disassembly, step 3, printed p.58

steps.title: Catch released with a hand on the slide
steps.action: Put on eye protection. Take a firm grip on the slide, pull it to the rear so the slide catch lever drops, and keep hold of it as it comes forward.
steps.prose: With the lever down, your hand is the only thing holding the slide against the recoil spring.
steps.quote:
Pull the slide to the rear to disengage the slide catch lever while maintaining control of the slide
assembly.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.1 Pistol Disassembly, step 4, printed p.59
steps.warn: FIREARMS CONTAIN SEVERAL SPRING LOADED PARTS. WEAR EYE PROTECTION AND MAINTAIN CONTROL DURING MAINTENANCE. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN INJURY.

steps.title: Slide assembly forward off the frame
steps.action: Guide the whole slide assembly straight forward and off the frame. The barrel and the recoil spring come with it.
steps.prose: Keep it level; tipping the slide as it leaves binds it on the rails.
steps.quote: Guide the complete slide assembly (slide, barrel, recoil spring, and guide) forward and off of the frame.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.1 Pistol Disassembly, step 5, printed pp.60-61

steps.title: Recoil spring guide assembly out
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Push the recoil spring guide forward a little, lift it from the rear, and take the assembly out in one piece.
steps.prose: Forward first, then up. SIG services and replaces this assembly as a single unit, so it stays together.
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring guide forward slightly and lift it from the rear to remove the recoil spring guide assembly from the slide.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.1 Pistol Disassembly, step 6, printed pp.60-61

steps.title: Barrel up slightly and back
steps.action: Lift the barrel a little and draw it to the rear, out of the slide.
steps.prose: It needs no force. If it will not move, the recoil spring guide is still in the way.
steps.quote: 7. Remove the barrel from the slide by pulling it upward slightly and to the rear.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.1 Pistol Disassembly, step 7, printed pp.60-61

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the slide, the barrel, the recoil spring guide assembly, and the frame in its grip module. A compensator, if yours has one, stays where it is. DEEP CLEAN carries the two jobs SIG publishes beyond this: the magazine apart, and the fire control unit out of the grip module.
steps.prose: The striker, the extractor and everything inside the slide stay put.
steps.quote: NOTE: This level of disassembly is sufficient for thorough cleaning after firing.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.1 Pistol Disassembly, note, printed p.61

steps.title: CLP patch from the chamber end, then let it soak
steps.action: Run a wet CLP patch down the barrel, in at the chamber and clear of the muzzle. Leave the CLP several minutes to loosen the residue and soften the carbon. If a compensator is installed, push the barrel forward in the slide first, to make room for the rod and patches.
steps.prose: The direction matters every time: chamber to muzzle. Work in moving air with eye protection on, and keep strong solvents off the outside of the pistol; they can harm the finish.
steps.caution: NEVER CLEAN THE BARREL FROM THE MUZZLE END. DO NOT USE A STEEL WIRE BRUSH AS IT CAN DAMAGE THE SMOOTH SURFACE OF THE BARREL.
steps.quote: Soak a patch with CLP and push it through the bore from the chamber end and out past the muzzle.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubricating, Barrel, printed p.65

steps.title: Brush, wet patch, dry patches
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the barrel with a cloth soaked in CLP. Run a second wet patch, scrub the heavy deposits with a bronze bore brush of the correct caliber on a rod, run another wet patch, then push dry patches through until they come out clean.
steps.prose: Light oil goes in the bore and chamber only if the pistol is going into storage, and it comes out again before the pistol is fired.
steps.quote: 9. Lightly oil bore and chamber if the pistol is to be stored for a period of time. 10. Always remove any lubricant from the bore prior to firing the pistol.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubricating, Barrel, printed p.65

steps.title: Extractor, rail slots and breech face
steps.action: Take off all the old lubricant first. Clean the slide with a cloth, then a soft brush and CLP where dirt and carbon have built up. Finish with a light coat of CLP in the slide's frame rail slots and a light film on the outside.
steps.prose: Keep oil out of the striker channel: SIG ties a wet channel to a light strike and a failure to fire.
steps.quote: Ensure the extractor, rail slots, and breech face are free of dirt and residue.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubricating, Slide Assembly, printed p.64
steps.warn: DO NOT LUBRICATE THE STRIKER OR ALLOW LUBRICANT TO FLOW INTO THE STRIKER CHANNEL OF THE SLIDE. THIS MAY CAUSE A LIGHT STRIKE TO THE CARTRIDGE RESULTING IN A FAILURE TO FIRE.

steps.title: Integrated compensator: nylon brush
steps.action: Only if your slide has a compensator built in: brush all the residue out of the compensator and off the front of the slide with a nylon brush. Leave the compensator where it is.
steps.prose: SIG says a compensator does not come off for routine maintenance and cleaning.
steps.quote: If the slide has an integrated compensator, use a nylon brush to remove all residue buildup from the compensator and the front of the slide.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubricating, Slide Assembly, printed p.64

steps.title: Recoil spring guide assembly, in one piece
steps.action: Clean the assembly with CLP and a soft brush, then put a light coat of CLP back on it.
steps.prose: If it is worn or damaged, the whole unit is replaced.
steps.quote: The P385 recoil spring and guide assembly should not be disassembled. It is serviced and replaced as a single unit.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubricating, Recoil Spring and Guide Assembly, printed p.66

steps.title: Rails, takedown lever, slide catch lever
steps.action: Wipe the frame and grip module with a soft cloth and get into the corners with cotton swabs. Put a light coat of CLP on the frame rails and on the working parts you can reach, and wipe the magazine well out with a soft cloth.
steps.prose: The rails, the takedown lever and the slide catch lever are the places SIG singles out.
steps.quote:
Use cotton swabs to clean hard to reach areas. Pay special attention to the frame rails,
takedown lever, and slide catch lever.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubricating, Frame Assembly and Grip Module, printed p.66

steps.title: The gap between the trigger and the trigger block
steps.action: Clean the trigger and look at the small block set into its face. Work out any grit or lint caught between the two.
steps.prose: The block has to move freely: the trigger is meant to stay locked unless the block is pressed with it, and debris in the gap gets in the way of that.
steps.quote:
Clean the trigger assembly and ensure any debris is removed between the trigger and trigger
block.
steps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 11.2 Cleaning and Lubricating, Frame Assembly and Grip Module, printed p.66

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off
deepSteps.action: With the magazine empty, use a punch or a similar tool to push the tab of the magazine insert forward and then down, and take the floorplate off. Keep a thumb over the insert as the plate clears it.
deepSteps.prose: The spring runs the whole length of the tube and is pushing on that insert. Eye protection on.
deepSteps.quote:
Using a punch or similar tool, push the tab of the magazine insert forward then down to release
and remove the floorplate.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 12.1 Magazine Disassembly, step 1, printed p.72
deepSteps.warn: FIREARMS CONTAIN SEVERAL SPRING LOADED PARTS. WEAR EYE PROTECTION AND MAINTAIN CONTROL DURING MAINTENANCE. FAILURE TO COMPLY MAY RESULT IN INJURY.

deepSteps.title: Spring and follower out of the tube
deepSteps.action: Let the spring out under control and take the follower and the spring out of the bottom of the tube. Note which way the follower faces.
deepSteps.prose: The follower goes back on the spring the same way round.
deepSteps.quote: 2. Remove the magazine follower and magazine spring from the magazine tube.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 12.1 Magazine Disassembly, step 2, printed p.73

deepSteps.title: Tube and follower
deepSteps.action: Wipe the tube and the follower with a cloth, then go over both with a soft brush and CLP. Clean the spring, the floorplate and the insert with a cloth.
deepSteps.prose: SIG puts most stoppages down to the magazine, so this is worth doing as carefully as the pistol.
deepSteps.quote: Wipe the magazine tube and follower with a cloth. Clean the magazine tube and follower with a soft brush and CLP.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 12.2 Cleaning, step 1, printed p.73

deepSteps.title: Light CLP on the spring and the outside of the tube
deepSteps.action: Put a light coat of CLP on the magazine spring and on the outside of the tube.
deepSteps.prose: Oil inside the tube ends up on the cartridges, and SIG says not to use cartridges that are dirty or wet.
deepSteps.quote: 3. Apply a light coat of CLP to the spring and outside of the magazine tube.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 12.2 Cleaning, step 3, printed p.73

deepSteps.title: Magazine back together
deepSteps.action: Set the follower on the spring and feed both into the bottom of the tube. Compress the spring until the insert is flush with the bottom of the tube, hold the insert there, and slide the floorplate onto the tube lips until the insert locks it.
deepSteps.prose: The floorplate has to be locked by the insert. Try to slide it back off by hand; it should not move.
deepSteps.quote: Holding the magazine insert in place, slide the magazine floorplate onto the magazine tube lips until the floorplate is locked in place by the insert.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 12.3 Magazine Assembly, step 3, printed pp.74-75

deepSteps.title: Fire control unit: slide off, lever up, pin out
deepSteps.action: With the pistol cleared and the slide assembly off the frame, make sure the takedown lever is rotated up, then use a punch or a similar tool to push the FCU pin out of the grip module.
deepSteps.prose: The barrel and the recoil spring guide do not have to come out of the slide for this. The pin goes back from right to left, so look at how it sits before you push it.
deepSteps.quote: 2. Ensure the takedown lever is rotated up. 3. Use a punch or similar tool to remove the FCU pin.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 18.1 FCU Removal, steps 2-3, printed pp.98-99

deepSteps.title: Lift and rotate the fire control unit out
deepSteps.action: Pull up on the frame rails and rotate the fire control unit up and out of the grip module. With it out, wipe the inside of the grip module with a soft cloth.
deepSteps.prose: It comes out in one piece. Look at the locking tab on the unit and the slot it sits in at the top of the trigger well; that tab goes into that slot when the unit goes back.
deepSteps.quote: 4. Pull up on the frame rails, and rotate the FCU up and out from the grip module.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 18.1 FCU Removal, step 4, printed pp.100-101

deepSteps.title: The fire control unit stays whole
deepSteps.action: Stop here. Nothing comes off the fire control unit itself, and nothing comes out of the slide: no striker, no extractor.
deepSteps.prose: Work past what this book explains goes to a certified SIG SAUER armorer.
deepSteps.quote: NO FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE FIRE CONTROL UNIT (FCU) IS AUTHORIZED.
deepSteps.cite: SIG P385® PISTOLS — OPERATOR’S MANUAL: HANDLING & SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS — P/N 5400232-01 REV 02 — 18.2 FCU Installation, caution, printed pp.100-101
deepSteps.warn: Disassembly beyond the instructions in the Operator’s Manual is restricted to a certified SIG SAUER Armorer.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Wet CLP patch from the chamber end out past the muzzle, then several minutes to soak
Outside of the barrel wiped with a CLP cloth, then a second wet patch
Bronze brush of the correct caliber on the heavy deposits, another wet patch, dry patches until clean
Compensator installed: barrel pushed forward in the slide to make room for the rod
Stored pistol: light oil in the bore and chamber
⛔ Never clean from the muzzle end and never use a steel wire brush
⛔ Never fire it with lubricant in the bore

cleaning.name: SLIDE ASSEMBLY
tasks: All the old lubricant off before any new goes on
Cloth, then a soft brush and CLP on dirt and carbon
Extractor, rail slots and breech face free of residue
Integrated compensator, if fitted: nylon brush, compensator left in place
Light CLP in the frame rail slots; a light film on the outside
⛔ Never oil the striker or let oil run into the striker channel

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING GUIDE ASSEMBLY
tasks: CLP and a soft brush, then a light coat of CLP
⛔ Never take it apart; it is replaced as a single unit

cleaning.name: FRAME AND GRIP MODULE
tasks: Soft cloth over the frame and grip module
Cotton swabs at the frame rails, takedown lever and slide catch lever
Light CLP on the frame rails and the working parts you can reach
Magazine well wiped free of dirt and dust
Debris out from between the trigger and the trigger block

reassembly: Deep clean only: fire control unit into the grip module, its locking tab fitted into the mating slot on the top of the trigger well.
Deep clean only: FCU pin pushed in from right to left, flush on both sides. The direction matters — pushing it from the other side can damage a spring in the frame.
Look through the barrel and make sure it is clear. Turn the slide upside down and put the barrel in.
Recoil spring guide assembly into the slide, with eye protection on.
Make sure the takedown lever is turned clockwise to its stop, then guide the slide onto the frame rails from the front.
Pull the slide fully back and lock it open with the slide catch lever. Turn the takedown lever counterclockwise until it stops.
Press the slide catch lever, or pull the slide back and let it go. Do not ride the slide forward.
fncheck:
Clear the pistol first and keep all ammunition away; the muzzle stays in a safe direction throughout. Insert an empty magazine: an audible click, and the catch holds it. Pull the slide fully back; the follower should lock it open. Press the magazine catch: the magazine must fall free under its own weight. Press the slide catch lever to close the slide.

Magazine disconnect, if fitted: pull the trigger with no magazine in — nothing should happen. Release it, insert an empty magazine and pull again — the striker should release with an audible click. Pull the slide fully back, then press the slide catch lever to let it forward.

Manual safety, if fitted: push it up and pull the trigger — the striker should NOT release. Release the trigger and push the safety down.

Pull the trigger to the rear and hold it: the striker should release with a click. Still holding it, pull the slide fully back and let it go, then release the trigger — a light click as it resets. Now pull at the edge of the trigger, without engaging the trigger block: the trigger should not go fully to the rear and the striker should NOT release. Pull with the block engaged: the striker should release with a click. Pull the slide fully back and let it go. Last, draw the slide back about 0.4 inch (10mm), or until the barrel hood drops out of the slide, and press the trigger: the striker should NOT release.

Never use a pistol or magazine that is damaged or fails any of this; SIG asks for it to be returned for evaluation.
